subject: ss-haematology
title: Marrow failure aplastic anaemia and PNH
refs: Harrison Principles of Internal Medicine 22e Ch 107 Bone Marrow Failure Syndromes
British Society for Haematology guideline on aplastic anaemia 2024

steps.tx: **Aplastic anaemia** (marrow failure with fatty replacement) strikes **2** per million yearly in Europe and up to **7** per million in Asia, hitting teens and older adults. **Pancytopenia** (all lineages low) with low reticulocytes and empty marrow defines it. **T cell** (cytotoxic immune cell) attacks on **CD34** (stem cell marker) progenitors drive most acquired cases. **Benzene** exposure, radiation and **posthepatitis** failure (after hepatitis) cover classic triggers.
steps.say: Aplastic anaemia replaces marrow with fat and drops all lineages. Immune T cell attacks cause most acquired cases. Benzene and hepatitis remain classic triggers.

steps.tx: Inherited failures arrive with clues. **Fanconi anaemia** (DNA repair defect) shows radial and skeletal deformities with chromosome breaks on **diepoxybutane** (DEB, breakage test) exposure. **Telomere biology disorders** (telomere shortening diseases) strike marrow, lung and liver together. **GATA2** (transcription factor) deficiency combines marrow failure, **NTM** (nontuberculous mycobacteria) and leukaemia risk. **Diamond Blackfan anaemia** (ribosome defect) isolates red lineage failure in infancy with thumb anomalies.
steps.say: Fanconi anaemia shows skeletal deformities and chromosome breaks. Telomere disorders strike marrow, lung and liver together. GATA2 deficiency combines marrow failure with mycobacterial infection.

steps.tx: **Myelodysplastic syndromes** (MDS, clonal marrow dysplasia) mimic aplastic anaemia but carry dysplastic (abnormally formed) precursors and clonal mutations. **Blast percentage** (immature cells) governs leukaemia progression, with **20** percent marking leukaemia. **IPSS** (International Prognostic Scoring System) and **IPSS M** (molecular version) stratify risk by blasts, cytogenetics and mutations. **Ring sideroblasts** (iron granule cells) with **SF3B1** (splicing mutation) mark low risk disease.
steps.say: Myelodysplasia mimics aplastic anaemia but carries clonal mutations. Ring sideroblasts with SF3B1 mark low risk disease. IPSS M stratifies risk with molecular data.

steps.tx: **PNH** (paroxysmal nocturnal haemoglobinuria, GPI anchor defect) arises from **PIGA** (phosphatidylinositol anchor gene) mutation on the X chromosome, losing **CD55** (decay accelerator) and **CD59** (protectin) proteins. Cells haemolyse intravascularly, especially in sleep, with **hemoglobinuria** (dark morning urine), pancytopenia and **thrombosis** (clots) in portal and cerebral veins. **Flow cytometry** (antibody cell test) for **FLAER** (reagent detecting missing anchors) confirms it.
steps.say: PNH loses GPI anchored CD55 and CD59 proteins from a PIGA mutation. Morning haemoglobinuria and venous thrombosis dominate. FLAER flow cytometry confirms the diagnosis.

steps.tx: PNH and aplastic anaemia overlap often, since immune attack selects PNH clones that escape T cell killing. **LDH** (cell damage enzyme) soars, **haptoglobin** (binding protein) vanishes and **reticulocytes** rise if marrow recovers. **Iron deficiency** develops from urinary iron loss. **Transfusion** is accepted but **eculizumab** (C5 complement blocker, terminal complement inhibitor) stops haemolysis, while **ravulizumab** (long acting C5 blocker) extends dosing intervals.
steps.say: PNH clones escape immune killing and often coexist with aplastic anaemia. Eculizumab stops complement haemolysis, and ravulizumab extends dosing intervals. Urinary iron loss causes iron deficiency.

steps.tx: Severe aplastic anaemia needs **IST** (immunosuppressive therapy) or **HSCT** (stem cell transplantation) by severity and donor availability. **Horse ATG** (antithymocyte globulin) with **cyclosporine** (calcineurin blocker) and **eltrombopag** (thrombopoietin mimic) lifts response above **90** percent. **Eltrombopag** (platelet growth mimic) stimulates all lineages and is used even in moderate disease. Matched sibling transplantation is preferred in young patients, while IST suits older adults.
steps.say: Horse ATG with cyclosporine and eltrombopag lifts response above ninety percent. Eltrombopag stimulates all three lineages. Matched sibling transplantation suits young patients best.

steps.tx: Supportive care decides survival while marrow recovers. **G-CSF** (granulocyte growth factor) bridges neutropenic infections, and irradiated blood prevents **TA-GVHD** (transfusion associated graft versus host disease). Fever with absolute neutrophil count below **500** needs immediate broad antibiotics. Transfusion thresholds favour platelets below **10**,000 and haemoglobin near **7** to **8** grams per decilitre in stable patients. **Growth factors** temper, but never replace, definitive therapy.
steps.say: Neutropenic fever needs immediate broad antibiotics. Irradiated blood prevents transfusion associated graft versus host disease. Growth factors bridge, but never replace, definitive therapy.

steps.tx: Leukaemic evolution haunts follow up. **MDS** (myelodysplasia) and **AML** (acute myeloid leukaemia) emerge in **10** to **15** percent after aplastic anaemia, especially with adverse clones. **PNH clones** expand without cancer in most patients, but monitoring continues. **Variceal bleeding** risks rise with thrombocytopenia and liver iron. Lifelong surveillance includes blood counts quarterly, clonal checks yearly and iron assessment in transfused patients.
steps.say: Leukaemic evolution follows aplastic anaemia in ten to fifteen percent. PNH clones usually expand without cancer. Lifelong counts and clonal surveillance remain mandatory.

steps.tx: Pregnancy and vaccination add nuance. PNH flares in pregnancy with thrombosis risk, so complement blockade continues and thromboprophylaxis is standard. **Meningococcal vaccination** (meningitis vaccine) must precede eculizumab, since C5 blockade invites meningococcal sepsis. **PIGA** is X linked but somatic in PNH, explaining female predominance. **Iron** supplementation corrects urinary losses once complement is controlled.
steps.say: PNH flares in pregnancy with high thrombosis risk. Meningococcal vaccination must precede complement blockade. Iron corrects urinary losses once haemolysis is controlled.

steps.tx: Rote numbers: aplastic incidence **2** to **7** per million; posthepatitis failure **5** percent; eltrombopag triple therapy response above **90** percent; MDS evolution **10** to **15** percent; blast threshold **20** percent for leukaemia; PNH marker **FLAER** by flow cytometry; and eculizumab every **2** weeks versus ravulizumab every **8** weeks. Never give non irradiated blood to severe aplastic patients.
steps.say: Aplastic anaemia strikes two to seven per million people. Triple therapy lifts response above ninety percent. Leukemic evolution follows in ten to fifteen percent of cases.
